notes: Qualification summary: Large North American utility; primary goal is to move critical inference workloads into a private VPC to meet regulatory & operational controls.
Primary workloads: control-room assistant (real-time), incident triage (low-latency), document search across operator manuals (embeddings + reranking).
Latency/throughput targets: 95th pct latency <= 120ms for control-room assistant; sustained throughput 1.5k tokens/sec during peak shift handovers; burst capacity for incident windows.
Model preferences: open Llama-3 variants fine-tuned on operator logs; fallback to smaller quantized variants for cost-sensitive paths. Must support quantization and KV-cache persistence.

Data residency: All PII and telemetry must remain in customer-selected regions (primary: us-east-1, secondary: eu-west-1 for DR). Logs must not cross regions unless encrypted with customer KMS and explicitly approved.
KMS / BYOK: Customer requires envelope encryption with customer-owned keys in Thales/EKM or AWS KMS with BYOK flow. Need guidance on key rotation, access controls, and HSM attestation.
Audit logging: Immutable audit stream forwarded to Splunk/Graylog with 7-year retention; must support signed logs and tamper-evidence. Redwood's audit hooks must map to internal event schema.

Network topology constraints: No public inbound endpoints. Preferred architecture: Private subnets for worker pools, Transit Gateway peering to Verdigris VPCs, control plane over private link or customer-managed VPN. Egress limited to specific registries and Redwood control-plane IPs over TLS 443.

Inbound/outbound rules specific asks: Allow outbound to S3 endpoints (for artifacts) and CRL/OCSP services; disallow arbitrary 3rd-party egress. Inbound only via AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering with strict source IP ACLs.

Security review progress: Initial architecture review completed 2026-02-24. InfoSec requested SOC2 report, KMS/HSM attestation, network diagram, and SIEM ingestion contract. Provided SOC2 and architecture; HSM attestation pending.
Quote from Verdigris Chief Architect: "We cannot have model inference traffic traverse public internet — all inference must be provably within our network or encrypted with our keys."

POC ask: 4-week POC. Week 1: network & IAM (VPC, subnets, KMS setup). Week 2: model onboarding + quantization tests. Week 3: latency/load tests & integration with Splunk. Week 4: security review handoff and runbook for failover to secondary region.
Operational requirements: RBAC with SAML/SCIM (Okta), token rotation, audit log forwarding, forensic export on-demand, SLA target for dedicated pool (99.9% inference uptime during shifts).
Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay premium for private deployment & compliance, but seeking Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization to control unit costs.

Open questions from Verdigris infra team: 1) How does Redwood handle model updates without exposing model artifacts to public buckets? 2) What is the recovery time objective (RTO) for cross-region fallback? 3) Can we bring our own NTP/time sources and maintain log timestamp integrity?
Next tactical items: deliver diagram + BYOK integration doc, fill HSM attestation gap, provide sample PrivateLink connection manifest, confirm feature parity for server-side cache invalidation.
Sales note: Strong executive buy-in (Head of Grid Ops). Legal has prepared initial draft with strict data residency clauses — procurement will push for 12–18 month committed billings if POC passes.
